standard_prerequisites: Flatness over a complete DVR detected by vanishing of uniformizer-power torsion
The presentation definition of locally Noetherian formal algebraic spaces, with etale transition maps between affines
Descent of representability and of the closed immersion property along etale surjective morphisms, from the spaces and bootstrap lemmas cited
core_obligations: Affine case: quotient out the uniformizer-power torsion to get B', and prove the universal property of X' = Spf(B') for maps from flat formal algebraic spaces using a presentation covering and the monomorphism property

Gluing: for the presentation {X_i to X}, the fibre products X'_i x_X X_j are flat over A, factor through X'_j, and the two identifications of R_ij agree because X'_i to X_i are monomorphisms of sheaves
Build the etale equivalence relation (U, R) with U the disjoint union of the X'_i, obtain X' = U/R as an algebraic space, and descend representability and the closed immersion property
Universal property in general: pull a flat Y back along the presentation, factor locally through X'_i, and descend along the etale covering
proof_roadmap: Construct the flat part in the affine formal case and verify its universal property locally
Check the compatibility of the local flat parts on overlaps and form the etale equivalence relation
Quote the presentation theorem for algebraic spaces and descend the closed immersion property
Prove the global universal property by etale descent
difficulty_reason: The counted conclusion is the existence and universal property of a closed immersion X' into a locally Noetherian formal algebraic space X over a complete DVR, representing the locus flat over A (source lines 5751-5829, label lemma-flat-locus). The solver must quotient torsion affinely, glue the local flat parts over the etale presentation via an etale equivalence relation, descend representability and monomorphism properties along etale covers, and finally establish the global universal property; the sheaf-level gluing with the monomorphism identification of the relation is a substantive argument. Allowed background: the presentation formalism and the cited spaces, bootstrap and formal spaces lemmas, delivered as navigation pointers.
